Read first: `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan/research/agent-rules-2026-11-20.md`.
Worktree `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/settings-hub`, branch `pilot/settings-hub`, base `717faf6`. Report: `research/settings-hub-report.md`. Boat run name: `settings-hub`.
You are the implementer (Sol). Scope: a structural UI change the owner has already approved (no feature flag; default taken, logged as L6). Tests cover the logic you add, not a sweep.

## Owner decisions (2026-11-20, verbatim intent)

- "I would like to unify all settings into one settings menu that is accessible from the top menu. This goes for the app appearance and theme as well."
- "I am unable to locate where to import." (Import is only reachable from a loose "Settings backup" text button above the real app bar.)
- Three icons stacked in the notification dashboard's corner are hard to use. After the mock-ups the owner said: "bottom bar works for me, the rest of what you have there sounds great."

## UI inheritance

| Source | Path or SHA | Take from it |
|---|---|---|
| Mock-up (signed off, v1) | research/settings-nav-mockups.html (copy in this worktree), section 1 (all three phones) and section 2 option A | layout, order, copy, icons (gear, inbox, flag, grid), group names, row labels, the unread badge, Export/Import as equal rows |
| Original screen | onboarding/onboarding_presentation/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/onboarding_presentaion/main/MainScreen.kt @ 717faf6 | top bar, the overflow DropdownMenu to remove, ShowcaseLayout showcase of the appearance menu, UiModeDialog/ThemeColorsDialog wiring and MainScreenEvent names |
| Original screen | app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/MainActivity.kt @ 717faf6 | Scaffold topBar "Settings backup" TextButton to remove; NavHost routes; theme state |
| Original screen | notification_filter/notification_filter_presentation/.../dashboard/NotificationDashboardScreen.kt, .../NotificationFilterScreen.kt (Inbox), .../apppriority/AppPriorityScreen.kt, .../settings/NotificationFilterSettingsScreen.kt @ 717faf6 | current top bars and the three icons (Tune, List, Settings) to replace; screen content stays |
| Original screen | app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsBackupActivity.kt @ 717faf6 | the export/import engine and flows; reuse, do not rewrite |
| Original screen | onboarding/.../components/UiModeDialog.kt, ThemeColorsDialog.kt, SelectAppearanceScreen.kt @ 717faf6 | the existing appearance and theme state, swatch colours and events; reuse their state and events, and the swatch drawing |
| Prior pilot / landed feature | 7ff936f (nav-bar padding on NotificationFilterScreen) and pilot/settings-portability @ 717faf6 | the bottom inset handling to keep correct (no double padding); the backup/restore engine and ProcessStores |
| Prior pilot / landed feature | core-ui/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/core_ui/components/AppBar.kt (CommonAppBar), notification dashboard widgets in .../dashboard/widgets/ | existing app bar and card styles; none found: Material 3 NavigationBar or BottomNavigation in the repo (searched `NavigationBar\|BottomNavigation` in all .kt files) |

## Fidelity check

Screenshot pairs (mock-up | build), same viewport 1080x1920 (the emulator) and the mock-up's phone frame width: `captures/settings-hub/` (create it). The host has no browser, so the mock-up cannot be rendered here: compare the build's screenshots against the mock-up's markup and CSS line by line (copy, order, icons, spacing relationships, which controls exist) and list every visible difference. A different model will do the fidelity review (`research/fidelity-review.md`) from your screenshots and the HTML; make that easy.

## What to build

1. Main dashboard top bar: title plus ONE gear `IconButton` (contentDescription "Settings") that navigates to a new `Routes.SETTINGS`. Remove the overflow `DropdownMenu` (About / Appearance / Theme colors) and the `MainActivity` Scaffold `topBar` "Settings backup" button, so there is one top bar. Point the existing appearance showcase (`shouldShowcaseAppearanceMenu`, `ShowcaseLayout` index 1) at the gear with new copy: appearance, theme and backup now live in Settings.
2. `Routes.SETTINGS`, a Compose screen: groups Look (Appearance as a three-way Light / Dark / System switch bound to the existing UI-mode state and event; Theme colors as swatches bound to the existing theme-colors state and event), Your data (Backup and restore, opens the next screen), Features (Usage, Notifications, Delayed launch: each opens its existing settings route `USAGE_SETTINGS`, `NOTIFICATION_FILTER_SETTINGS`, `DELAYED_LAUNCH_SETTINGS`), About (opens `ABOUT_APP`). Use `CommonAppBar` style for the back button and title. The dialogs (`UiModeDialog`, `ThemeColorsDialog`) may stay if the onboarding `SelectAppearanceScreen` still needs them; remove their use from the main screen.
3. `Routes.BACKUP_RESTORE`: copy from the mock-up; Export settings and Import settings as two equal rows. They open `SettingsBackupActivity` with an explicit action extra (export or import) that starts that flow immediately; without the extra the activity behaves as today. Put the extra parsing in a small pure function with a JVM test.
4. Notification area bottom bar: one scaffold shared by the notification dashboard (Overview), the Inbox and App priorities (Apps), using Material 3 `NavigationBar` with labelled items Overview (grid icon), Inbox (inbox icon, badge = unread count from the existing dashboard counts) and Apps (flag icon). The top bar of these three screens keeps back and the screen title and has exactly one action: the gear to `NOTIFICATION_FILTER_SETTINGS`. Remove the three corner icons from `NotificationDashboardScreen`. Tab switching uses `launchSingleTop`, `restoreState` and a `popUpTo` of the area's start so Back leaves the area in one press; keep the existing deep link on `NOTIFICATION_FILTER`. Share one unread-count source between the bar and the screens (a ViewModel scoped to the area's nav entry), no second query.
5. Insets: the bottom bar owns the bottom inset. The inbox's pinned Clear All button (7ff936f added `navigationBarsPadding()` to its container) must sit above the bottom bar with no double padding, on 3-button and gesture navigation.
6. Accessibility: contentDescriptions on every icon-only button, 48dp touch targets, NavigationBar labels always shown, selected state announced.
7. Icons: use `androidx.compose.material.icons` if the extended set is a dependency; otherwise add vector drawables from the mock-up's SVG path data (gear, inbox, flag, grid, palette, mode, down, up, info, clock, chevron). One icon per concept; the gear means Settings only.

## Out of scope (do not touch)

The Inbox rows and the dashboard widgets' content (a separate display-language study is under way); the per-category Clear All behaviour (branch `fix/clear-per-category` edits the same button area of `NotificationFilterScreen`: keep your edits there minimal so the two merge); the snooze work; any settings schema.

## Tests and evidence

Pure logic gets JVM tests (the intent-extra parsing, the badge text for 0, 1, 99, 100+ unread if you format it, tab selection from a route). Compose layout is verified by screenshots. Run `:app:assembleDebug`, `:app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin` and the unit tests of modules you touch. Emulator: the shared AVD (see the rules; check `adb devices`), install the debug APK, capture: main top bar, Settings, Backup and restore, notification Overview / Inbox / Apps with the bar, on light and dark appearance, with 3-button navigation (`adb shell cmd overlay enable com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.threebutton`). Put the PNGs in `captures/settings-hub/`. State in the report which differences from the mock-up remain and why.

Start immediately. About five minutes in the orchestrator will read your files and question your choices.

## Decisions and verification

- L6. Ship the approved UI directly, with no feature flag.
- Preserve Inbox as the entry tab for the Farhan dashboard card and existing notification deep link. Overview and Apps sit alongside it.
- Existing tests changed: none.

- The Inbox retains its existing settings showcase anchor, including the gear when notification access is off. Overview and Apps use the same app bar style and destination.
- Backup rows use the same card styling and height rules. Launches with an explicit action run it after the existing outcome check. A pending outcome must be acknowledged before automatic launch. Activity recreation restores only an action that has yet to start.
- Badge display is hidden at zero and capped at `99+`. Accessibility uses the full count. Dynamic theme colors still require Android 12.

    colorStyle: ThemeColors,

) {

    val colorScheme = when (colorStyle) {

                )

            }

My verdict is **fix first**. The structure matches the signed-off mock-up, but the bottom bar the owner asked for is the wrong colour family on all three notification screens.

I rendered the mock-up with headless Chromium on Boat at 360×800, scale 3, and made side-by-side pairs (mock-up | build) for all 12 screenshots. The mock-up has only one dark palette, so its light and dark renders came out identical. Its text shows in a serif font because the page relies on font variables from its original host; ignore that. Boat reported 0% hours left after this, so I stopped using it.

**Your four points:**
- **(a) Lavender bar: confirmed.** `NotificationArea.kt` creates `NavigationBar { … }` without setting a colour, so it falls back to `surfaceContainer`. `Theme.kt` never passes that colour into any of its six colour schemes, although `Color.kt` defines it (`surfaceContainerLight = 0xFFF6EDDF` and so on). The bar's pixels are exactly the Material 3 defaults: `#F3EDF7` in light, `#211F26` in dark. The gap in the theme is older than this branch; the bar is just the first full-width thing that shows it. The mock-up's bar has no fill: it uses the page background with a thin line on top.
- **(b) Clear All overlap: not new.** At 717faf6 the button already floated over the list, with 72 dp of bottom padding so the last card can scroll clear. The branch only removed the old bottom padding because the bar now handles it. The button's white text on peach is also from the base and has poor contrast.
- **(c) Appearance control: your premise is wrong, and the build matches.** The caption says "three-way switch", but the markup is a three-segment control (Light / Dark / System). That is what the build draws. The real problem is that in light mode the selected segment is `#E6E8DC` on white, so you can barely see which one is on. The author's report doesn't mention this.
- **(d) Apps tab:** not flagged.

**Inheritance:** the build reuses the original appearance and theme state, the dashboard cards, the dashboard widgets, the inbox rows, the existing app bar and the backup engine. None of it was rebuilt; the report quotes the code. One leftover: `UiModeDialog` and `ThemeColorsDialog` are no longer used anywhere, but their state fields and events remain.

**Top 3 fixes:**
1. **Bottom bar:** use the page background with a thin divider on top, as in the mock-up. Fixing the missing colours in `Theme.kt` is the real cure, but it would recolour every dialog and menu in the app, so it should be a separate follow-up.
2. **Selected appearance segment:** use the theme's green (`secondaryContainer`), which matches the mock-up's highlight and the bar's selected pill.
3. **Accent colours:** make the group headings `secondary` green (readable in both modes; today they are near-black in light and gold in dark). Make the badge amber instead of error red. Also fix the gold backup-row titles in dark mode.

Two things for the owner to decide rather than fix: the notification area opens on Inbox while the mock-up shows Overview selected, and the mock-up highlights the Import row while the build makes Export and Import identical.

Files are in `/home/mini/Documents/repos/Farhan.worktrees/settings-hub`:
- `research/fidelity-review.md`
- `captures/settings-hub/pairs/` (side-by-side pairs)
- `captures/settings-hub/pairs/mockup/` (mock-up renders)

content.text:
Short answers below. Measuring point 4 overturned my own fix 2, and the grep in point 1 changes what I recommend for fix 1. I edited nothing.

**1. Bar colour.** Setting `containerColor = colorScheme.background` and adding a `HorizontalDivider(color = outlineVariant)` uses only theme tokens, so it isn't theming around the app in the hard-coded-hex sense. But it does override a shared control's default to cover a gap in the theme, and the gap stays everywhere else. Since the grep shows the gap is wider than the bar, the fix belongs in `Theme.kt`, and I withdraw the override.

Grep (Material 3 1.3.1, from BOM 2025.02.00):
- **Explicit reads:** no app code reads `surfaceContainer*` directly.
- **Material defaults that read it, outside tests:**
  - 11 `AlertDialog` (reads High), in 7 files across app, core-ui, notification_filter, onboarding and usage_overview.
  - 9 `DropdownMenu` (reads `surfaceContainer`).
  - 2 `DatePickerDialog`, 1 `DatePicker` and 2 `TimePicker` (High).
  - 1 `ModalBottomSheet` and 1 `BottomSheetScaffold` (Low).
  - About 16 `Switch` calls, whose off-state track reads Highest.
  - The new `NavigationBar`.
- **Plain `Card`s:** the two that don't pass colours are covered. `MainScreenCard` sets `primaryContainer` (it measures `#E6E8DC`), and the Inbox rows paint their own background. So no visible card changes.

All of these show Material's baseline lavender today, so wiring the tokens corrects every one; none of them gets worse. The change is mechanical: `Color.kt` already defines the five `surfaceContainer*` values for every scheme, and wiring them adds about 30 lines to `Theme.kt`. The shifts are subtle: in light, the bar goes from `#F3EDF7` to `#F6EDDF` and dialogs from `#ECE6F0` to `#F0E7D9`. It's cheap enough to do now, checked with screenshots of one dialog, one menu, an off switch and the bar, in light and dark. After that the default bar fits the theme. What remains differs from the mock-up only in being a tonal bar instead of flat with a hairline, which can be recorded as a deliberate Material default.

**2. Badge.** The amber is made up for the mock-up. It is `--app-warn:#e6b35a` in the mock-up's `:root` block, not a theme token. Classic `tertiary` is teal (`#0C6B59` light, `#85D6BF` dark), and the only amber-ish token is `primary` `#EAB466`, which is close by coincidence. Keep Material's error red. I drop this fix.

**3. What the owner sees in the first 10 seconds:**
1. **Bar colour.** It shows on every notification screen, next to cream cards and a green pill. Fix now with the `Theme.kt` wiring.
2. **The area opens on Inbox, not Overview.** The owner signed off on a picture with Overview selected. This needs one line in the handoff explaining why, not a code change.
3. **Light mode: you can't tell which appearance option is selected.** This is visible as soon as the owner opens Settings in light mode. Fix now (see point 4 for how).

Leave as follow-ups (only visible side by side, or not from this branch):
- heading colour (they read as bold labels and don't look broken)
- gold backup titles in dark mode
- Import emphasis
- the unused dialogs
- Clear All's white on peach (1.87:1), which comes from the base and belongs on `fix/clear-per-category`.

**4. Segment contrast (WCAG ratios):**

| Pair | Now | With `secondaryContainer` |
|---|---|---|
| Selected fill vs unselected, light | `#E6E8DC` on `#FFFFFF`: **1.24:1** | `#CBEEA5` on `#FFFFFF`: **1.29:1** |
| Selected fill vs background, dark | `#222317` on `#000000`: 1.32:1 | `#334E17` on `#000000`: 2.24:1 |
| Selected label on its fill | 13.81:1 | 13.31:1 |

My fix fails by the number. In light it changes the hue, not the contrast, and both are below the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 asks for state indicators. The fill colour can't carry the selected state on its own. Material 3 1.3.1's `SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow` puts a checkmark on the selected segment, and the checkmark carries the state. Switching to that replaces the hand-built control with a shared one. If a fill alone is wanted, `secondary` `#4A672D` with white text is 6.42:1.
